original_title: Precise Iodide‐Trap Strategy for Photothermally Stable Spiro‐OMeTAD‐Based Perovskite Solar Cells
title: Trapping the iodide that kills spiro-OMeTAD perovskite cells
blurb: Heat and light let iodide wander out of the perovskite and de-dope the spiro-OMeTAD hole transporter, wrecking the interfacial contact that keeps these cells working. A dual iodide-trap additive, built around a tetrafluoroiodobenzamide, catches the wandering ions and keeps hole transport and interface intact under photothermal stress. Stability engineering rather than another efficiency record, which is the part perovskite cells actually need.

original_title: On-Column Preparation of High-Performance Affinity Chromatography Columns
title: Building affinity chromatography columns without packing them separately
blurb: An on-column route to high-performance affinity chromatography columns, forming the stationary phase in place rather than packing pre-made resin.

original_title: Bis(2‐Adamantyl)Magnesium: Synthesis, Structure, and Applications of a Versatile and Shelf‐Stable 2‐Adamantyl Anion Equivalent
title: A shelf-stable anion for the adamantyl position nobody uses
blurb: 1-adamantyl gets all the attention because its cation is trivial to form, leaving the 2-adamantyl position, and anionic building blocks for it, largely undeveloped. Bis(2-adamantyl)magnesium is offered up as a stable, practical 2-adamantyl anion equivalent, opening substitution at the bridge carbon instead of just the bridgehead.

original_title: Mimicking Enzyme Activation Within an Ionic Liquid‐Immobilized Coordination Capsules for Electroreduction of N 2 to NH 3
title: An enzyme-mimicking capsule for squeezing NH3 out of N2
blurb: Electrochemical N2-to-NH3 reduction usually stalls on poor efficiency and selectivity. Here a redox-reversible helical capsule uses hydroxyl groups lining its interior to encapsulate an N2-associated ionic liquid, pre-organizing the substrate the way an enzyme active site would before pushing the reduction through. Clever mimicry, though it's still a capsule in a beaker.

original_title: Standardized FDG-PET interpretation during CAR T-cell therapy in R/R DLBCL: a DESCAR-T study
title: Getting everyone to read the post-CAR-T PET scan the same way
blurb: A DESCAR-T study working out a standardized way to interpret FDG-PET scans in relapsed or refractory DLBCL patients after CAR T-cell therapy, the unglamorous consistency check that multi-center data actually depends on.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Rhodium/copper dual catalysis for defluorinative annulation of gem-difluorocyclopropanes with phenols
title: Rh/Cu tag-team turns difluorocyclopropanes into benzofurans
blurb: Gem-difluorocyclopropanes ring-open and couple with phenols under combined rhodium and copper catalysis, shedding both fluorines along the way to build 2-methylbenzofuran derivatives directly. Using the C–F bonds as a leaving group rather than fighting to keep them is the neat part.

original_title: MUHC launches world’s first radioligand therapy trial for HER2-positive cancers - McGill University
title: First radioligand therapy trial aimed at HER2-positive cancers
blurb: MUHC has opened what it's billing as the world's first radioligand therapy trial specifically for HER2-positive cancers. It's their claim to the "first," so worth waiting to see how the arms actually read out.

original_title: Unperturbed π‐Methyl Electrostatic Interactions Enable Efficient Toluene Adsorption on Graphdiyne Under High Humidity
title: Graphdiyne keeps eating toluene even when the air's humid
blurb: Humidity usually beats out VOCs for adsorption sites, but a hydrophobic graphdiyne framework holds onto over 98% of its toluene uptake (102.5 mg/g) at 50% relative humidity with stable cycling, where conventional carbon adsorbents degrade. Credited to π-methyl electrostatic interactions between the framework and toluene's methyl group, which apparently don't care that water's competing for the same spots.

original_title: Crosslinked hybrid micellar platform for targeted cutaneous drug delivery.
title: Crosslinked micelles aimed at delivering drugs through skin
blurb: A crosslinked hybrid micellar platform built for targeted cutaneous drug delivery.

original_title: Novartis invests 140 billion won to build RLT hub in South Korea - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
title: Novartis parks 140 billion won on a radioligand therapy hub in South Korea
blurb: No trial data or new molecule here, just capacity: Novartis is building out an RLT manufacturing hub in South Korea, another node in the buildout everyone's racing on the back of Pluvicto-style demand.

original_title: Machine Learning-Assisted Evolution of Broadly Functional Enzyme Libraries
title: ML picks the starting enzyme so directed evolution doesn't have to guess
blurb: Directed evolution lives or dies on having a starting protein with a whisper of the promiscuous activity you actually want, and finding that starting point is usually the bottleneck, not the evolution itself. This uses machine learning to screen for those faint activities across enzyme libraries and hand directed evolution a real starting line instead of a blind search.

original_title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Induced Switching of Interaction Hierarchy in Dipolar D–A Chromophores for NIR Circularly Polarized Photodetection
title: Hydrogen bonds flip these NIR dyes from chiroptically dead to circularly polarized
blurb: Dipolar donor-acceptor chromophores default to packing head-to-tail with their electrostatic complement, which kills any chiroptical signal. Bolting amide hydrogen bonds onto a croconaine-based dye overrides that preference and forces homo-association instead, and that packing switch is what turns on circularly polarized NIR photodetection. A supramolecular packing trick, not a new chromophore.

original_title: Co‐Localization‐Gated Multivalent DNA Logic Gate for Programmable Cell Recognition
title: A DNA logic gate that only fires when two markers land on the same cell
blurb: Split DNAzyme modules sit on a tetrahedral DNA scaffold and only reconstitute their peroxidase-mimicking activity when two adjacent modules co-localize on one target cell, an AND gate enforced by physical proximity rather than affinity alone. The point is fewer off-target hits than binding-based recognition gives you.

original_title: Antibacterial Hydrogel Dressing With Ca(2+)-Dependent Hyaluronidase Responsiveness for Accelerating Wound Healing via On-Demand Release of AIE Photosensitizers.
title: A wound dressing that waits for hyaluronidase before it releases its payload
blurb: A hydrogel dressing keeps its AIE photosensitizer locked up until calcium-dependent hyaluronidase activity triggers release, dosing the antibacterial payload on demand instead of dumping it all at once. Framed as accelerating wound healing, though no performance numbers to go with the design.

original_title: Reprogramming Coiled-Coil Design Principles To Create Cross-α Peptide Filaments
title: Flip one face of a coiled-coil and you get cross-alpha filaments instead
blurb: Coiled coils are among the most designable motifs in protein engineering, and this inverts the hydrophobic face of a type II heptad repeat to redirect that same design toolkit toward cross-alpha filaments. AlphaFold-Multimer screened candidate sequences, and one design, ROX-LL, self-assembled into monomorphic alpha-helical filaments confirmed by cryo-EM. Less a new material than proof that the design rules bend if you invert the right face.

original_title: Antibody-drug conjugates against multidrug-resistant cancers: Biomarker-guided patient selection, payload engineering, linker chemistry, and bystander effects
title: A field guide to fixing ADCs when resistance sets in
blurb: A review rounding up the levers for antibody-drug conjugates against multidrug-resistant cancers: picking patients by biomarker, engineering the payload, tuning the linker chemistry, and leaning on bystander killing. No new data here, just the state of the field laid out in one place.

original_title: High-yield reactor production of terbium-161 using thin-layer gadolinium-160 targets, simplified chloride based separation and radiolabeling of DOTA based ligands
title: A high-yield route to terbium-161
blurb: Reactor-produced Tb-161 from thin gadolinium-160 targets, with a simplified chloride-based separation and radiolabeling worked out for DOTA ligands. A supply-chain paper, but that's the unglamorous work any therapeutic isotope needs before someone can actually dose it at scale.

original_title: Anti-TROP2 Antibody Drug Conjugates in EGFR-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Biological Rationale and Clinical Challenges
title: TROP2 as the next move after EGFR TKIs stop working
blurb: A review laying out why TROP2 is a live target once EGFR-mutant NSCLC progresses past its TKIs, and where the anti-TROP2 ADCs built for that setting actually run into trouble in the clinic. Rationale plus a reality check, not new trial data.

original_title: FAIMS-GPF XL-MS: crosslinking-mass spectrometry based on gas-phase fractionation
title: Gas-phase fractionation to catch the crosslinks XL-MS usually misses
blurb: FAIMS-based gas-phase fractionation bolted onto crosslinking mass spec, aimed at the weak, transient protein-protein interactions that standard XL-MS workflows tend to lose. A methods paper, but PPI mapping lives or dies on catching exactly these low-abundance crosslinks.

original_title: Synthesis Based on Covalent Capture and Release Enables Purification-free Fluorogenic Probe Libraries for Single-Molecule Protease Activity Profiling.
title: Fluorogenic probe libraries without the purification step
blurb: A covalent capture-and-release synthesis route that skips purification entirely, built to generate fluorogenic probe libraries for single-molecule protease activity profiling. Mostly a chemistry-logistics win: more usable probes, faster, for the single-molecule assays downstream.

original_title: Palladium-103 as a Theranostic Auger Electron Emitter: From Cyclotron Production to Preclinical SPECT Evaluation in Murine and Canine Models
title: Palladium-103 goes from cyclotron to dogs
blurb: Pd-103 made via the 103Rh(p,n)103Pd reaction on a cyclotron, then separated, purified, radiolabeled, and run through preclinical SPECT in both mice and canine models. It's an Auger emitter, so the whole pitch is nanometer-scale energy deposition, and this is the workflow paper trying to make that production-to-imaging pipeline actually scalable.

original_title: Advancing antibody drug conjugates in gastrointestinal cancers
title: Where ADCs stand in GI cancers
blurb: A review tracking antibody-drug conjugates as a treatment approach across gastrointestinal cancers.

original_title: Bioorthogonal epigenetic anchoring of heterochromatin to the nuclear lamina reverses senescence and osteoarthritis.
title: Locking heterochromatin back to the nuclear envelope undoes senescence
blurb: Bioorthogonal chemistry tethers heterochromatin back to the nuclear lamina, and that alone is enough to reverse senescence markers and osteoarthritis in the model used. If chromatin positioning is really driving the aging phenotype rather than just following it, that's the bigger deal here, not the anchoring trick itself.

original_title: Altruist Biologics' Hangzhou Antibody-Drug Conjugate Facility Receives Provincial Regulatory Approval for Segmented Production - The Manila Times
title: Altruist Biologics gets the green light on ADC manufacturing in Hangzhou
blurb: Provincial regulators approved segmented production at Altruist Biologics' Hangzhou ADC facility. A manufacturing-approval story, not a data one, worth filing away for capacity rather than clinical results.

original_title: Counteranion-mediated dynamic kinetic asymmetric fluorination to access sulfur-stereogenic center
title: Enantiocontrol finally reaches the S(VI)-F bond
blurb: A one-pot dynamic kinetic asymmetric fluorination builds sulfonimidoyl fluorides with direct control over the new sulfur stereocenter, run under mild conditions with a counteranion doing the steering. These are useful click linkers for drug discovery, and stereoselective access to the S(VI)-F bond has apparently been the sticking point until now.

original_title: AcTFirst Trial Design for Actinium-225 PSMA-617 in Taxane-Naive mCRPC - Oliver Sartor - UroToday
title: Actinium-225 PSMA-617 moves earlier, before taxanes
blurb: Sartor's writeup lays out the AcTFirst trial design: testing Ac-225 PSMA-617 in mCRPC patients who haven't had taxane chemo yet, pushing the alpha emitter up the treatment line instead of saving it for later. Just the design here, no readout.

original_title: Topological Crosslinker Design Regulates Interfacial and Active Species Transport in Zinc-Iodine Batteries.
title: A crosslinker redesign to keep zinc-iodine batteries from shorting themselves
blurb: The pitch is a crosslinker whose topology controls how ions cross the interface and how the active iodine species get shuttled around, aimed at zinc-iodine batteries. Journal listing only, so no numbers to back the claim yet.

original_title: Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor radiotheranostics for imaging activated tumor stroma and guiding radionuclide therapy.
title: FAP-targeting radiotracers for the stroma around the tumor, not the tumor itself
blurb: A review on fibroblast activation protein inhibitor radiotheranostics, imaging the activated stroma tumors build around themselves and using that signal to guide radionuclide therapy. Field roundup, not new data.

original_title: A biocatalytic platform for the stereoselective synthesis of diverse atropisomeric compounds using engineered metalloenzymes
title: Engineered enzymes take atropisomer synthesis past the usual biaryls
blurb: Biocatalytic atropisomer synthesis has mostly meant C-C biaryl axes. This platform uses engineered metalloenzymes to hit other atropisomer classes stereoselectively, which is the actual news since biocatalysis barely touches this space otherwise.

original_title: Gentamicin-Linked Supramolecular Hybrid Hydrogels: Mechanically Robust Cucurbit[7]Uril-Based Networks for Prolonged Infection Control.
title: A gentamicin hydrogel held together by cucurbit[7]uril
blurb: Supramolecular networks built on cucurbit[7]uril host-guest chemistry, loaded with gentamicin and pitched as mechanically robust enough to hold up for sustained infection control. No mechanical or release numbers given, just the design.

original_title: Emrelis for c-Met Positive NSCLC: A Breakthrough in Antibody-Drug Conjugate-based Treatment Approved by the FDA
title: Teliso-V: an ADC for c-Met positive lung cancer that doesn't need MET signaling to work
blurb: Telisotuzumab vedotin pairs an anti-c-Met antibody with MMAE on a cleavable linker, so the payload lands on c-Met-overexpressing tumor cells without depending on MET signaling for effect. It shrank xenografts that had already resisted other MET-targeted drugs, and it's now FDA approved as Emrelis for c-Met positive NSCLC.

original_title: Catalytic Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral Indole‐Fused Medium and Large Rings: A Burgeoning Field
title: Building chiral indole-fused medium and large rings enantioselectively
blurb: A review of the recent push to close indole-fused medium and large rings asymmetrically, a construction that's stayed underexplored because these ring systems are just hard to make enantioselectively. Field roundup rather than one result.

original_title: Electrochemical cross-electrophile coupling for carbon–heteroatom and heteroatom–heteroatom bond formation
title: Cross-electrophile coupling goes electrochemical, and past carbon-carbon
blurb: Electrochemical cross-electrophile coupling extended to carbon-heteroatom and heteroatom-heteroatom bond formation, where the method's usually been a C-C tool. Journal listing only, no yields to judge it by.

original_title: Photocatalytic Radical Functionalization of Alkenylammonium Salts
title: Alkenylammonium salts as radical acceptors nobody had bothered with
blurb: Photoredox catalysis, paired with halogen or hydrogen atom transfer to generate the alkyl radicals, adds them across these electron-deficient cationic alkenes to build quaternary ammonium compounds under mild conditions. They demonstrate it with cyclopropanation and late-stage functionalization, so the scope looks genuinely broad rather than one showcase reaction.

original_title: Enhertu® Approved in the EU as First Tumor Agnostic HER2 Directed Therapy and Antibody Drug Conjugate for Patients with Previously Treated HER2 Positive Metastatic Solid Tumors - BioSpace
title: Enhertu goes tumor agnostic in the EU
blurb: EU approval for Enhertu as the first tumor agnostic HER2-directed ADC, cleared for previously treated HER2 positive metastatic solid tumors regardless of where the cancer started. The approval is riding on the biomarker, not the organ.

original_title: Plasma-enhanced catalytic CO₂ hydrogenation: Experimental investigation of Ni-based catalysts performance and techno-economic feasibility compared to conventional thermal systems
title: Plasma-boosted CO2 hydrogenation, but does it pay for itself
blurb: Ni catalysts on alumina, ceria, and zirconia supports, run thermal-only versus plasma-coupled across 200-450C, 1-10 bar, and H2:CO2 ratios from 2:1 to 4:1, with a techno-economic comparison against conventional thermal reactors bolted on. The economics are the actual point here, since plasma setups always look good on conversion and less good once you price the extra power draw.

original_title: Using enantioselective biosensors to evolve asymmetric biocatalysts
title: Skip the chromatography, let the cell report its own enantiomeric excess
blurb: Engineered transcription factors that turn an enzyme's enantiomer ratio directly into a gene-expression signal, built for imine reductases and screened with a massively parallel reporter assay across more than 300,000 variants with full dose-response curves. That's aimed at the actual bottleneck in evolving chiral biocatalysts, which was never the catalysis, it was always the slow chromatography needed to check what came out.

original_title: Influence of Head‐to‐Tail Cyclization of Lanmodulin‐Inspired Peptides on Lanthanide Affinity and Structure
title: Closing the loop on lanmodulin-inspired peptides for rare-earth binding
blurb: Head-to-tail cyclized versions of lanmodulin-inspired EF-hand peptides, checked against lanthanides by TRLFS, ITC, and NMR to see whether locking the peptide into a ring changes affinity and structure versus the linear ones. The end goal is rare-earth separation and recycling, where peptide binders are still the underdog against solvent extraction.

original_title: Application of 2D‐Chromatography System for the Determination of Cosmetic Peptides in Skin Homogenates
title: Tracking cosmetic peptides as skin enzymes chew through them
blurb: A 2D-chromatography method built to measure how cosmeceutical peptides hold up against dermal protease degradation in skin homogenates. The field has been selling peptide actives on stability without much data actually measuring it, which is the gap this fills.

original_title: Ceramic-based microfluidic and mesoscale reactor systems: applications and perspectives
title: Ceramic microreactors for the chemistry that eats plastic tubing
blurb: A review making the case for ceramic microfluidic and mesoscale reactors over the usual polymer platforms, which fall apart under hot, corrosive conditions. It's a perspective piece, so the case for switching materials rather than new data.

original_title: Interim PET response of Pola-R-CHP predicts outcome in previously untreated CD5-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a multicenter retrospective study
title: Interim PET as an early readout for Pola-R-CHP in CD5-positive DLBCL
blurb: A multicenter retrospective from China, 32 previously untreated CD5-positive DLBCL patients (median age 63.5, most already stage II or higher) given Pola-R-CHP first-line, checking whether the PET/CT after 3 cycles tracks how they end up doing. CD5-positive is the aggressive, poor-prognosis subtype, so an early readout that actually holds would be useful, assuming it survives past 32 patients.

original_title: Protein-Polysaccharide Complexes as Delivery Systems for Quercetin: Mechanisms, Microstructure, and Applications in High-Protein Beverages
title: Wrapping quercetin in protein and polysaccharide so it survives a protein shake
blurb: A review of protein-polysaccharide complexes as carriers for quercetin, tackling its usual problems (poor solubility, heat sensitivity, low bioavailability), with the new angle being formulation specifically for high-protein beverages rather than the usual food matrices. Summarizes mechanisms and microstructure, no new data of its own.
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

original_title: Coordination Chemistry of Boron Subphthalocyanine With BINOL Derivatives: Unexpected Oxidation to Oxa[4]Helicene and Properties of the Resulting Axially Coordinated Complexes Containing Oxa[4]Helicene and/or BINOL Derivatives
title: BINOL misbehaves and hands you an oxa[4]helicene instead
blurb: Pairing boron subphthalocyanine with BINOL as a chiral axial ligand was supposed to just bolt chirality onto an achiral macrocycle, but the BINOL got oxidized and ring-closed into an oxa[4]helicene instead, and they characterized the resulting axial complexes anyway. A synthesis that wandered off plan into a more interesting structure.

original_title: Frustrated Lewis pairs engineering via dopant-defect coupling in quantum dots for spatial regulation of proton and electron utilization in CO2 photoreduction to oxygenated products
title: Doping frustrated Lewis pairs into quantum dots to steer CO2 toward oxygenates
blurb: Cu doping in CdS quantum dots creates Cu+ and adjacent vacancy pairs that act as frustrated Lewis pairs, setting up local electric dipoles that separately route protons and electrons during photocatalytic CO2 reduction. The point is fixing the usual tradeoff where separating redox centers cuts charge recombination but starves the proton transfer needed to get past CO to actual oxygenated products.

original_title: Nickel catalysis enables chemoselectivity in radiation chemistry
title: Nickel catalysis brings some order to radiation chemistry's radical soup
blurb: Borrowing the radical-tuning trick from metallaphotoredox chemistry, a nickel catalyst system reins in the chemoselectivity problem that's dogged using ionizing radiation to activate inert molecules, since radiation alone just throws off whatever radicals it feels like. A neat crossover between two fields that don't usually talk, if the selectivity holds up past whatever substrates they tried.

original_title: Assembly of Molecular Chromophore–Catalyst Assemblies on Metal Oxide Semiconductors by Metal–Ligand Coordination Chemistry
title: One anchor group does two jobs: hangs the dye and holds the catalyst
blurb: Phosphonic acid-tagged Ru(II) polypyridyl dyes bind straight to a metal oxide surface, and the same phosphonate groups double as a ligand that clamps a dinuclear cobalt catalyst onto the dye itself. Surface loading of dye versus catalyst is set just by how protonated the phosphonic acid is, a cheap knob for building photoelectrodes without a separate catalyst-deposition step.

original_title: A Comparative Study of the Influence of Water and Temperature on the Racemization of Five‐ and Six‐Membered l ‐Alanine‐Derived Imides
title: Blame the DMF, not the imide, for the racemization
blurb: Water slowly hydrolyzes DMF into dimethylamine and formic acid, and that extra amine base is what pulls the alpha proton and racemizes the L-alanine-derived imide, worse with more water and more heat. Six-membered imides hang onto their stereocenter better than five-membered ones and throw off fewer side products, so ring size is the practical lever if you're stuck running these reactions wet and hot.

original_title: Metal–Oxide Interface for Heterogeneous Catalysis via Intensifying Activation of Reactant Molecules
title: A review's case for why the metal-oxide boundary is doing the real catalytic work
blurb: A review across alcohol oxidation, CO oxidation, soot combustion, CO2 hydrogenation, dry reforming, and alkane conversion, arguing the metal-oxide interface itself is the active site: it keeps two different reactants from competing for the same spot and lets each activate on the surface it actually prefers. Useful as a survey of the mechanistic argument, but it's a review, so don't expect a single new number out of it.

original_title: Polyesterification-assisted interface engineering of carboxylate metal-organic frameworks membranes for selective gas separation
title: Sealing MOF membrane grain boundaries with an in-situ polyester bond
blurb: UiO-66 membranes leak selectivity through grain boundaries and interfacial defects, so this adds triethanolamine during synthesis and heats it to trigger localized polyesterification right at those boundaries, anchoring polymer across the gaps instead of leaving them open. The idea is a self-standing, MOF-rich membrane where the defects get chemically stitched shut rather than just tolerated.

original_title: IN SITU SYNTHESIS Of HIERARCHICAL MOF/LDH NANOCOMPOSITES FOR ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL MATERIALS
title: MOF/LDH composites made the standard way
blurb: Coprecipitation plus solvothermal synthesis grows MOF/LDH hybrids with some control over particle size and crystallinity, pitched for better adsorption and catalysis. Long on tunability claims, short on any actual numbers, so it reads as a materials-recipe paper rather than one with a result to point to.
venue: Journal of Baku Engineering University Physics

original_title: Is the problem of immunogenicity for drug delivery vehicles practically solved such that significant percentage of population is not affected?
title: Is the problem of immunogenicity for drug delivery vehicles practically solved such that significant percentage of population is not affected?
blurb: I am aware that research suggests that PEG (poly(ethylene glycol)) used in drug delivery vehicles is not as anti-immunogenic as previously thought, partially due to its prevalence in other products and hence a large portion of human population has developed anti-PEG antibodies. (Edit: Even then I have heard that automatic clearance of PEG is not permanent for much of population.) Thus, work into other non-immunogenic polymers such as PCB, that is, poly(carboxybetaine), poly(sulfobetaine), poly(2-oxazoline), etc is being done and so far I have self-researched specifically about PCB. Most papers

original_title: An Enzymatic Platform for Late‐Stage (Radio)isotope Labelling of Oligonucleotides With Methyltransferases
title: An enzyme swaps in the radiolabel for oligonucleotide ADME studies
blurb: Methyltransferases installing (radio)isotope labels late-stage on oligonucleotides, aimed squarely at the tritium-labeling bottleneck that ADME and whole-body autoradiography studies depend on, a route that's normally slow, expensive, low-specific-activity, and generates a lot of radioactive waste. If the enzymatic swap holds up broadly it fixes a genuinely annoying supply problem, not just a nicer paper.

original_title: Evaluation of [(225)Ac]Ac-PSMA-617 vis-a-vis Rechallenge [(177)Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 PRLT Versus Cabazitaxel or Oral Metronomic Chemotherapy in mCRPC: An Observational Analysis of Outcome and Toxicity Profiles in a Real-World Clinical Scenario.
title: Comparing what you throw at mCRPC once PSMA therapy runs its course
blurb: A real-world observational look at second-line options for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, pitting Ac-225-PSMA-617 against Lu-177-PSMA-617 rechallenge, cabazitaxel, and oral metronomic chemo on outcomes and toxicity. Retrospective and observational, so it's hypothesis-generating rather than a head-to-head trial.

original_title: Therapeutic Outcomes of (177)Lu-DOTATATE Targeted Therapy in Patients with Medullary Thyroid Cancer: A Case Series of 10 Patients.
title: Lu-177-DOTATATE tried on medullary thyroid cancer, ten patients
blurb: A case series testing Lu-177-DOTATATE outcomes in medullary thyroid cancer, a tumor type it's not the usual target for. Ten patients is enough for a case series and nothing more.

original_title: PSMA and Integrin α(v)β(3) Dual-Targeted Radioligands for Prostate Cancer Targeted Radionuclide Therapy.
title: A radioligand that hits PSMA and integrin αvβ3 in prostate cancer
blurb: Dual-targeted radioligands built to engage both PSMA and integrin αvβ3 at once for prostate cancer radionuclide therapy, aimed at tumor cells that get by on reduced PSMA expression. Medicinal-chemistry design and characterization work, ahead of any clinical read.

original_title: PSMA and Integrin α v β 3 Dual-Targeted Radioligands for Prostate Cancer Targeted Radionuclide Therapy
title: One ligand, two receptors: PSMA plus integrin αvβ3 for prostate cancer
blurb: Same dual-targeting logic, a radioligand built to hit PSMA and integrin αvβ3 together so PSMA-low tumor cells don't get a free pass. Still at the med-chem characterization stage, not patients yet.

original_title: Synthesis and Characterization of Radio-Halogenated Talazoparib Analogues for Imaging and Radioligand Therapy.
title: Putting a radiohalogen on Talazoparib for PARP imaging and therapy
blurb: Radio-halogenated analogues of the PARP inhibitor Talazoparib, synthesized and characterized as candidates for both imaging and radioligand therapy, riding on the same PARP-avid scaffold that already works as a drug. Early synthesis and characterization, no in vivo data mentioned yet.

original_title: In Situ Click Chemistry Forming pH/ROS-Responsive and Antifouling Hydrogel to Prevent Intrauterine Adhesion and Restore Fertility.
title: A click-chemistry hydrogel to stop the uterus from scarring shut
blurb: An in-situ-forming hydrogel made by click chemistry, tuned to respond to pH and ROS and built to resist fouling, meant to sit in the uterus after injury and keep the walls from fusing back together while it degrades. The pitch is preventing intrauterine adhesion and preserving fertility.

original_title: Chemical Modification Strategies for Therapeutic Oligonucleotides: Mechanism Compatibility, Design Trade-Offs, and Translational Barriers
title: The state of chemically patching up oligonucleotide drugs
blurb: A review of how chemical modifications to oligonucleotide therapeutics trade off against each other, nuclease resistance, clearance, delivery, endosomal escape, off-target activity, and immune recognition all pulling in different directions with no single fix for all of them. A map of the constraints more than a new result.

original_title: Substituent-rebound skeletal editing for precise boron-to-carbon single-atom swapping
title: Swapping a boron for a carbon inside an aromatic ring, one atom at a time
blurb: A single-step reaction that swaps a boron atom for a carbon within an aromatic scaffold via a substituent-rebound mechanism, leaving the peripheral substituents untouched so the effect of that one atom change can be isolated. Single-step methods for this kind of atom swap are rare, which is the actual point.

original_title: Re: Köylüce N et al. Predictive Value of Pre-treatment Ga-68 PSMA-11 PET/CT Volumetric Parameters for Toxicity in Lu-177 PSMA-617 Therapy.
title: A reply on whether pretreatment PSMA PET can predict Lu-177 toxicity
blurb: A commentary responding to a study that used pretreatment Ga-68 PSMA-11 PET/CT volumetric parameters to predict toxicity risk ahead of Lu-177-PSMA-617 therapy, weighing in on whether that predictive claim actually holds.

original_title: Radiometal-labelled derivatives of olaparib do not permeate cell membranes
title: Radiolabeled olaparib still can't get through the cell wall
blurb: Tag olaparib with a radiometal to image PARP-1 and you'd want it inside the nucleus, but these derivatives just don't cross the cell membrane at all. A flat negative result, useful mainly as a warning to anyone eyeing the same chelation strategy.

original_title: Dynamic Binding of Alkali‐Metal Ions in a Metalloporphyrin Cage: Impact on Redox Catalysis
title: Tuning a cobalt porphyrin cage's redox chemistry by which cation it's holding
blurb: Alkali metal cations parked inside a cobalt porphyrin cage shift the Co1+/Co0 redox potential, with K+ and Cs+ pushing it hardest, up to 236 mV, and that in turn moves the cage's CO2 reduction activity. A synthetic stab at the kind of second-sphere electrostatic control enzymes already exploit, which catalyst design usually ignores.

original_title: Mechanochemical Diastereoselective Substrate-Directed Synthesis of Pyrrole-Isoxazolidines via 1,3-Dipolar Cycloaddition of Maleimides with Nitrones
title: Ball milling makes the pyrrole-isoxazolidine diastereomer you actually want
blurb: A mechanochemical take on the maleimide-nitrone 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition, with the substrate itself steering which diastereomer comes out. Not much more to go on than that title.

original_title: Enhanced HGF with increased receptor affinity and nitration-dysfunction resistance through interaction with lipoic acid trisulfide
title: A sulfur trick makes HGF resistant to the damage that aging normally does to it
blurb: Aging piles up reactive nitrogen species that nitrate and disable HGF, but treating it with lipoic acid trisulfide (LASSS) at a 1:8000 ratio produces a form that binds c-Met more than twice as well and shrugs off that same nitration, protecting tyrosine 198 more than 250. A modified growth factor that's better, not just intact.

original_title: Ancillary Ligand‐Controlled Dinitrogen Cleavage and Transformation at Titanium Centers
title: Swap the ancillary ligand, get a different fate for N2 at titanium
blurb: Same PCP-titanium scaffold, but aryloxide or diarylamide ligands push all the way to full N-N cleavage into a bis(mu-nitrido) dititanium complex, while the plain phenyl version activates a C-P bond instead. Splitting N2 with a 3d metal is rare enough on its own, and here it's the ligand choice doing the steering rather than brute reactivity.

original_title: Circular Photocaged mRNA for Light‐induced Late‐stage Activation of Translation
title: A circular mRNA that stays dark until you hit it with light
blurb: Click chemistry circularizes the mRNA by tagging the 5' cap and 3' poly-A tail with bioorthogonal handles, sidestepping circular RNA's usual problem of having no cap and translating poorly. The payoff is a construct that resists the exonuclease chewing that kills linear mRNA's half-life, and stays untranslated until a light pulse switches it on late-stage.

original_title: Organometallic Chemistry Approach to Peptide Tricycles
title: Stapling peptides into tricycles with organometallic chemistry
blurb: A Bioconjugate Chemistry piece on building tricyclic peptide scaffolds, the multi-loop extension of the bicycle-binder idea, using organometallic chemistry to do the stapling. Thin on specifics beyond that.

original_title: Quantitative relationship between microdosimetric quantities and plasmid DNA damage induced by auger electrons.
title: Putting numbers on how Auger electrons chew up plasmid DNA
blurb: A quantitative link between microdosimetric quantities and the actual DNA damage Auger electrons inflict on plasmids. Useful for anyone trying to predict Auger damage from dose rather than just measuring it after the fact.

original_title: Guiding principles for seeded electrochemical synthesis of multimetallic nanocrystals
title: Seed the crystal first, then grow the multimetallic shape you wanted
blurb: Plain electrodeposition tends to hand you ill-defined, aggregated nanocrystals, so this seeds the growth and matches it to lattice mismatch and metal-metal bond energy instead. That control gets you core-shell, multilayered, or hollow multimetallic architectures on purpose, via electrochemical pathways you can actually program rather than hope for.

original_title: Auger Electron Therapy Enhanced by Heat-Triggered Release of I-125-Labeled DNA-Targeted Compounds within the Tumor Microenvironment
title: A heat switch to dump Auger-emitting iodine-125 right in the tumor
blurb: I-125-labeled DNA-targeted compounds are held back and released only when heat triggers them inside the tumor microenvironment, boosting the Auger electron therapy that follows. The logic is concentrating a short-range emitter exactly where it can reach DNA, though the snippet doesn't give much past that setup.

original_title: Selective pore modulation in layered molecular crystals
title: Two pore sizes, tuned independently, in the same framework
blurb: Triskele-shaped building units give hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks two distinct pore types you can dial in separately instead of fighting over one shared pore. Load the result with superacids and it comes out both acid-stable and a decent proton conductor.

original_title: Tridentate Ligand Enabled Pd(II)-Catalyzed Nondirected C(sp2)–H Deuteration of Highly Electron-Deficient Arenes.
title: A ligand that gets Pd to deuterate arenes nobody wants to touch
blurb: A tridentate ligand packing a terminal donor, central donor, and internal base into one scaffold lets Pd(II) swap C-H for C-D on electron-deficient arenes using D2O as the deuterium source, no directing group required. Broad substrate scope, good functional-group tolerance, and it's pitched as beating the current best catalysts, handy for late-stage labeling.

original_title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Annulations of an Anti‐Bredt Olefin
title: Getting a strained bridgehead alkene to actually react
blurb: Anti-Bredt olefins are notoriously hard to use in synthesis because the ring strain that makes them interesting also makes them unstable. Here two short-lived species, both generated in situ at low concentration, get united through Pd catalysis with a [2.2.1]-bridged bicyclic ABO instead of just decomposing before they can meet.

original_title: Catalytic Hydrosulfenylation of Maleic Anhydride and Its Derivatives Enabled by Proton-Coupled Electron Transfer
title: Hydrosulfenylation of maleic anhydride, PCET style
blurb: A proton-coupled electron transfer route to catalytic hydrosulfenylation of maleic anhydride and its derivatives. Not much more to go on than that framing.

original_title: Considerations for Recycling of Acetonitrile in Oligonucleotide Synthesis
title: Trying to stop pouring acetonitrile down the drain
blurb: A look at recycling the acetonitrile burned through in oligonucleotide synthesis. No recovery numbers given, just the premise that it's worth reclaiming.

original_title: Concise Chemoenzymatic Total Synthesis of 14-Membered Cyclophane-Type Peptides
title: Making burpitides to order instead of foraging plants for them
blurb: These 14-membered cyclophane peptide alkaloids have mostly stayed unstudied because plant sources are scarce and the chemistry to make them is hard. A chemoenzymatic route built around an ancestrally reconstructed enzyme gets four of them, lotusine A, spinachristene A, nummularine F, and mauritine C, in just 10-11 steps from L-proline.

original_title: Bigger Molecules Enter Smaller Channels of Zeolites via Inward-Coil-Alike Adaptation
title: Molecules folding themselves to fit zeolite pores too small for them
blurb: Bulkier guest molecules getting into narrower zeolite channels than their size should allow, apparently by coiling inward to adapt on the way through. That's the whole pitch as far as the snippet goes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Enediyne Chimeras for Targeted NAMPT Degradation: Enhancing Cytotoxicity via a Radical Clock
title: Enediyne warheads repurposed as NAMPT degraders
blurb: Chimeric enediynes built to degrade NAMPT, with a radical clock wired in to push cytotoxicity higher. Not much detail beyond that design choice.

original_title: Phase Engineering of Fe-Polyoxometalate Sub-1 nm Assemblies for High-Efficiency Photoelectrocatalytic Nitrogen Reduction
title: Shrinking iron polyoxometalates below a nanometer for nitrogen fixation
blurb: Phase-engineered Fe-polyoxometalate clusters under a nanometer in size, aimed at photoelectrocatalytic nitrogen reduction. No efficiency numbers here, just the sub-1nm and phase-engineering angle as the claimed lever.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Enantioselective Construction of Spirocyclohexadienones Via NHC-Catalyzed Formal [5 + 1] Annulation Reaction of Dienals
title: NHC catalysis builds spirocyclohexadienones one enantiomer at a time
blurb: A formal [5+1] annulation of dienals under NHC catalysis, run enantioselectively, to build the spirocyclohexadienone core. No yields or ee numbers to go on beyond that.

original_title: Radiosynthesis and Preclinical Evaluation of Enantiopure ( R )-[ 18 F]Fluorolactate for PET Imaging of Metabolic Processes
title: A PET tracer that tells R from S in lactate
blurb: Enantiopure (R)-[18F]fluorolactate, radiosynthesized and run through preclinical PET imaging to track lactate metabolism. Animal work only so far, nothing on humans yet.

original_title: Comprehensive experimental validation of Monte Carlo model for imaging plate response to <sup>198g</sup>Au and interference from <sup>196g</sup>Au in the gold activation method
title: Untangling two gold isotopes in neutron fluence counting
blurb: The gold activation method reads neutron fluence off imaging plates via 198g-Au, but 196g-Au tags along and muddies the response. This validates a Monte Carlo model of that plate response against actual experiment to sort out how much signal is which isotope.

original_title: Engineering Frustrated Packing of Porous Organic Cages for Precision Acetylene–Ethylene Separation
title: Packing defects as the deliberate pore in porous organic cages
blurb: Porous organic cages get separation power from more than their built-in cavities, the gaps between packed molecules matter too. This engineers that intermolecular packing on purpose for acetylene/ethylene separation, instead of leaving it to whatever crystallization happens to give you.

original_title: Dynamic Coordination-Enabled Metal-Dependent Configurational Switching in a Covalent Organic Framework
title: Swap the metal, flip the framework
blurb: A covalent organic framework whose configuration switches depending on which metal it's coordinated to, dynamic coordination chemistry doing structural work in a COF rather than just holding the lattice together.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Anionic Passivation Enables Reconstruction-Free Seawater Electrolysis
title: A coating that stops phosphide catalysts from rebuilding themselves in seawater
blurb: Nonoxide phosphide catalysts are good at seawater oxidation but reconstruct and corrode at the anodic potentials the job requires. Growing an ultrathin, undercoordinated TiOx layer on a FeNiP support via Lewis acid-base interactions passivates the surface enough to stabilize the phosphide lattice without giving up the activity it was chosen for.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Functionalization‐Mediated Synthesis of Bridge‐Coordinated Fe Atoms on MoS 2 Nanosheets for PEM Water Electrolyzers
title: Bridging Fe atoms onto MoS2 for PGM-free hydrogen catalysts
blurb: A functionalization route pins bridge-coordinated Fe atoms onto MoS2 nanosheets, chasing a platinum-free HER catalyst for PEM electrolyzers. Spectroscopy and electrochemistry back the activity gains, but the field's usual sticking point, long-term stability, isn't the thing being claimed here.

original_title: Emerging Mechanisms and Synthetic Potential of Nonheme Fe(II)/α-Ketoglutarate-Dependent Dioxygenases
title: What nonheme Fe(II)/α-KG oxygenases are good for now
blurb: A survey of nonheme Fe(II)/α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, the enzyme family behind a wide range of oxidative transformations, and where their mechanisms are starting to get borrowed for synthesis. Reads like a review rather than a new result.

original_title: Reactivity of Alkali Metal Yldiides towards Carbon Disulfide
title: Ylides plus CS2 make isolable dithiolate salts
blurb: α-metalated ylides react with carbon disulfide to give CS2 adducts stable enough to isolate and solve by crystallography. The C-C bond comes out short in the solid state, meaning the structure leans hard into the 1,1-dithiolate form rather than staying ylide-like, and they also check whether these can be pushed further to alkynyl sulfide anions.

original_title: Site-Specific Tyrosine Sulfation of Triabin via Semi-Synthesis Enhances Thrombin Inhibition through Synergistic Multiple-Mode Interactions
title: Sulfating one tyrosine on Triabin to tighten its grip on thrombin
blurb: Semi-synthesis installs a sulfate on a specific tyrosine of Triabin, and that single change boosts thrombin inhibition through several binding modes acting together rather than one interaction carrying the effect.

original_title: Enantioselective Hydroarylation via Chiral Transient Directing Groups: Access to Chiral Benzo-Fused Heterocycles with Collaborative Enantiomeric Control
title: Two chiral controls working together on one C-H bond
blurb: A chiral transient directing group steers an enantioselective hydroarylation, with the directing group and catalyst apparently cooperating on enantiocontrol to build chiral benzo-fused heterocycles.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Catalytic Asymmetric Metallocyclopropanation Reactions Using Chloroform as a Carbyne Equivalent
title: A carbyne equivalent that's just chloroform
blurb: Asymmetric metallocyclopropanation using chloroform to stand in for a metal carbyne, skipping the usual carbyne-precursor fuss. Snippet's just the journal name, so that's the whole pitch.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Cobalt‐Catalyzed Reductive Asymmetric Dimerization of 1,3‐Enynes: Rapid Synthesis of Enantioenriched Skipped 1,3,6‐Trienes
title: First direct route to enantioenriched skipped trienes
blurb: A cobalt-catalyzed reductive cross-dimerization stitches two 1,3-enynes together into skipped 1,3,6-trienes with controlled stereochemistry, straight from simple starting materials. The authors say nobody had a direct route to these with stereocontrol before, so that's the actual news here.

original_title: Cu(I)-Catalyzed 6- endo - dig Annulation of 2-Bromoaryl Enaminones with Terminal Alkynes: Amine Exchange and Modular Access to Enamine Naphthalenones
title: Cu(I) turns bromoaryl enaminones and alkynes into naphthalenones
blurb: A 6-endo-dig annulation of 2-bromoaryl enaminones with terminal alkynes, with an amine-exchange step built in, gives modular access to enamine naphthalenones. Thin on detail beyond that.

original_title: Five more radioligand therapy sites under development at AON - Stock Titan
title: AON tacks on five more radioligand therapy sites
blurb: A press release, so just the headline number: five more radioligand therapy sites now in development at AON, no data behind it yet.

original_title: Cu-Catalyzed Regio- and Diastereoselective Propargylic Substitution of N -Hydroxyphthalimide Esters: Access to Propargyl-Containing N,O -Acetal Derivatives
title: Cu propargylic substitution builds N,O-acetals with an alkyne handle
blurb: Copper-catalyzed, regio- and diastereoselective propargylic substitution of N-hydroxyphthalimide esters gives propargyl-containing N,O-acetal derivatives. Snippet's just the journal name, so that's the extent of it.

original_title: DNA-Alkyne-Chain Probes Enable N-Glycosite-Resolved GlycoBarcoding of Cell-Surface Proteins
title: DNA-alkyne probes barcode glycosylation site by site
blurb: DNA-alkyne-chain probes tag individual N-glycosites on cell-surface proteins, giving a glycobarcoding readout resolved down to the specific site rather than an averaged glycan profile.

original_title: Highly scalable, dialysis-controlled synthesis of colloidal molecules via regulated self-assembly of polymer-grafted gold nanoparticles
title: Dialysis dials in how gold nanoparticles snap into colloidal molecules
blurb: Long-range electrostatic attraction paired with short-range hydrogen bonding, tuned via dialysis, self-assembles polymer-grafted gold nanoparticles into colloidal molecules that actually replicate real molecular symmetry. The pitch is scalability, going after the bottleneck that's kept these things a lab curiosity instead of a building block.

original_title: Operando High-Energy X-Ray Scattering Studies of Pt/Al 2 O 3 Catalysts during LOHC Dehydrogenation
title: Watching Pt/Al2O3 catalysts work in real time under LOHC dehydrogenation
blurb: Operando high-energy X-ray scattering on Pt/Al2O3 during LOHC dehydrogenation. Journal name is about all the snippet gives up.

original_title: VERAXA Biotech Announces Advancement of Novel Bispecific Antibody Drug Conjugate Program VXA-222 from Joint Discovery Collaboration with OmniAb - NTB Kommunikasjon
title: VERAXA's bispecific ADC VXA-222 moves forward
blurb: VXA-222, a bispecific antibody-drug conjugate out of VERAXA's discovery collaboration with OmniAb, advances to the next stage. It's a press release, so no data yet, just the milestone.
